********* clinic note      */*/****     11: 00 am      i had a telemedicine visit with mr. and ms. ****** today and spoke with ms. ******. she stated that mr. ****** appears better today though still very weak. he had an appetite today, but he is not eating as much as she would like him to eat. he is currently being treated for c diff.    the last time i met with mr. and mrs. ****** in person in our surgical clinic, we de discussed scheduling him for an elective interval laparoscopic appendectomy, possible open. i discussed the procedure at length with them, including the risks and benefits, and the very real chance that we may end up converting this to an open laparotomy. he has a pretty sizeable umbilical hernia which had become more prominent given how much weight he has lost recently. the hernia is directly over where we would usually place one of our laparoscopic ********. our goal would be to avoid this site and approach the appendectomy laterally. however, there is a chance that the hernia may impede our operative exposure and we may have to take it down to be able to access the appendix. this scenario would invariably increase the length and complexity of the operation, and the chance of converting to open.       mr. ****** was understandably anxious about surgery at that point and wanted some time to think about it so he can decide if he wanted to proceed or not. he and his wife were concerned about his fitness for the procedure.  although i did not do a formal frailty assessment at that time, he looked quite frail to me. given that there is a direct association between level of frailty and post-operative outcome, i ********* it would be helpful to have his cardiologist, and his pulmonologist do a formal risk assessment and clearance for surgery prior to moving forward. that would help the patient and his wife with the decision to proceed or not, and would also help the peri-operative team, including our 
anesthesiology colleagues, prepare to provide him optimal care, should he decide to move forward. in my experience with medically complex elderly patients undergoing elective surgeries, having a multidisciplinary input like this leads to the best outcome for these patients. i also contacted our anesthesiology colleagues to do a pre-operative assessment and, at their suggestion, referred mr. ****** to the *** preoperative optimization of senior health (****) clinic. he was seen at the **** clinic and a multidisciplinary ***ting was held thereafter to discuss the results of the evaluation. i took part in that ***ting.    i shared the results of the multidisciplinary ***ting with ms. ****** today. the consensus from the ***ting was that mr. ****** was very frail and at high risk of post-operative mortality, post-operative complications, and discharge to a destination other than home. based on my assessment of his medical history and my in-person evaluation, i agree with this consensus. it is my opinion, based on the available evidence, that at this time, the risks of the operation far outweigh the benefits and moving forward would be detrimental to the patient. i discussed with ms. ****** that there is a small chance that the infection might come back and if that were to happen, he could be treated with antibiotics and percutaneous drainage, assuming there were an abscess. the other reason to do an interval appendectomy was for the small possibility that a tumor (benign or malignant) could have obstructed the appendix and triggered the infection in the first place. if that were the case, mr. ****** would be unable to tolerate a colectomy and/or subsequent chemotherapy.     ms. ****** shared that both she and her husband have come to the realization that he is too frail to have an operation and her husband has made it clear that he does not want to have an operation, given that he has been though a lot already. i let 
her know that they are always welcome to have a second surgical opinion, either through our group which i can help them arrange, or with a surgeon outside our group which his pcp can help them arrange. ms. ****** stated that while she *********** this suggestion, she is quite happy with the thorough multidisciplinary evaluation that her husband has already had and that they are happy with the current recommendation. i let her know that she is always welcome to call our office with any questions or concerns and i would be happy to reach out and discuss these.    **** *********, md  #*****
